sources.entry: sish - HTTP(S)/WS(S)/TCP tunnels to localhost using only SSH (serveo/ngrok alternative). MIT Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: sish is an open-source SSH server that exposes local HTTP(S), WS(S), TCP, alias, and SNI-routed services to the internet using plain SSH tunneling, with no custom client needed.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes sish as an SSH server focused on forwarding and multiplexing. Users create tunnels with standard ssh -R commands, and sish routes HTTP(S), WS(S), and raw TCP traffic to them. It supports private TCP aliases reachable only through authenticated SSH (via ssh -J), and SNI-based routing of TLS traffic to multiple backends without terminating TLS. It also lists optional load balancing for HTTP/TCP/SNI aliases, a service console for inspecting forwarded requests, and key and password authentication with dynamic key reloading. A managed service at tuns.sh is mentioned as an alternative to self-hosting.
use_cases: Share a local web app over HTTPS with a public URL
Expose a local TCP service such as SSH on a remote port
Create private TCP aliases reachable only through SSH
Route TLS traffic by SNI to multiple backends
Self-host a serveo or ngrok-style tunneling service
how_to_run: git clone git@github.com:antoniomika/sish.git && cd sish && make dev
notable: Uses plain SSH clients (ssh -R, ssh -J), so end users need no custom software
Private TCP aliases reachable only through authenticated SSH
SNI routing of TLS traffic without terminating TLS
Distributed as binary releases and Docker images
Sponsored by pico.sh; a managed service at tuns.sh is available
caveats: Self-hosting requires a domain, DNS setup, and TLS certificate directory configuration
The README's managed service (tuns.sh) is a separate hosted option, not the self-hosted software itself
Local development points testing.ssi.sh at localhost, which is specific to the project's dev setup
